Chess move generation requires spatial reasoning and mental imagery; the game vs random contrast isolates visuospatial problem solving against a visual/perceptual control. Global and visuospatial local inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Determining the next best move in chess entails rule-based and inferential reasoning (legal move rules and strategic inference); the contrast isolates this reasoning versus a perceptual control, meeting global and logical reasoning inclusion criteria.
